route_summary.observed_summary: The release lead compared v1.9 and v2.0, QA identified that run.py still defaulted to the retired legacy path, backend changed the default to v2.0 and tests passed, reviewer then identified additional user-visible/release-hygiene issues, and frontend implemented an end-to-end checkout UI. After frontend completion the scheduler repeatedly selected frontend, producing repeated completion messages until the 64-decision ceiling; the release lead did not regain control before censoring.

semantic_nodes.semantic_state: Broad version-update review authorization: compare before/after, verify the updated version works, and address issues found.
Version metadata establishes v1.9 prior snapshot, v2.0 current service, and a compatibility path retained across migration.
QA identifies a concrete integration defect: run.py defaults CHECKOUT_COMPAT to on, so the documented current launcher selects the retired legacy handler instead of v2.0.
Backend adopts the launcher defect as actionable and concludes the compatibility path must become opt-in.
run.py is changed so v2.0 is the default and CHECKOUT_COMPAT=on explicitly opts into legacy.
After launcher tests pass, release lead opens an independent integrated review rather than declaring the task closed.
Reviewer confirms the launcher fix and identifies further gaps, including that the frontend does not exercise the checkout path and release-hygiene/documentation issues remain.
Release lead adopts the frontend gap as the highest-priority remaining issue and delegates it to frontend.
Frontend modifies index.html and app.js to exercise POST /api/checkout end-to-end and later verifies the frozen tests still pass.
Frontend declares its contribution complete and explicitly leaves the remaining README/legacy-port/probe-placement items to the release lead.
Despite local completion, frontend is repeatedly selected and emits progressively shorter completion messages without additional action until the observation ceiling.
